name: forward_global_with_stack_slot

name: call_library_function_minus_348

name: format_message_then_emit

name: copy_longs_then_call_handler

name: start_program_parse_arguments

name: call_indirect_and_return_result

name: call_library_function_minus_198

name: scan_for_marker_word

name: advance_past_encoded_entry

name: compute_word_branch_target

description: Calls the library routine at offset minus 210 through a base pointer held in a global variable, and returns with no result.

name: call_library_function_minus_414
description: Calls the library routine at offset minus 414 through a base pointer held in a global variable, and returns with no result.

name: call_library_function_minus_444
description: Calls the library routine at offset minus 444 through a base pointer held in a global variable, and returns with no result.

name: call_library_function_minus_450
description: Calls the library routine at offset minus 450 through a base pointer held in a global variable, and returns with no result.

name: call_library_function_minus_552
description: Calls the library routine at offset minus 552 through a base pointer held in a global variable, and returns with no result.

name: format_message_and_output
description: Formats a message into a 140-byte stack buffer with the format routine held in a global function slot, then measures the text. When it is not empty, it passes the text, its length and the incoming parameter to another routine.

name: store_low_byte_at_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of the data register to the byte location addressed by the address register, and returns.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiled code is bad instruction data: it ORs a byte into memory and then stops, so there is no meaningful routine to describe.

name: build_quoted_command_and_run
description: Zeroes a block of about 2,400 longs, allocates working memory when the stack is too small, and reads state from the current task and library base. It then builds a buffer holding a quoted copy of a text string and passes it on to library routines.

name: release_install_task_resources
description: Saves its incoming value in a per-task record, then conditionally calls cleanup routines and finally closes a library. Depending on the record's fields it also frees memory, forbids multitasking, replies to a message, and calls a routine at offset minus 732 when the version is above 35.

name: run_install_step_sequence
description: If the stack has enough room, runs a sequence of helper steps that look up and copy values and call library routines, returning zero on success or twenty on failure. Otherwise it moves to a fresh stack area 500 bytes lower, copies a string there and calls a library routine at offset minus 348 before running the same routine again.

name: check_disk_space_for_install
description: Allocates a memory block and locks a directory to read its disk information through library calls, then compares the free space with a required size. It returns one when enough space is available and zero otherwise, and it moves to a fresh stack area when the stack is low.

name: find_entry_by_code
description: Scans a table of 16-byte entries and returns the first whose code field equals the parameter and whose flag byte is non-zero, or zero if none match. When the stack is too low it moves to a fresh stack area 500 bytes lower, copies a string and calls a library routine at offset minus 348 before retrying.

name: process_install_table_entries
description: Walks a table of 16-byte install entries and, for entries with code 2 or 4, looks up a name and performs a copy and library calls, stopping at the first failure. It returns one on success and zero otherwise, and when the stack is low it moves to a fresh stack area and retries.

name: copy_file_in_chunks
description: Copies a file in blocks of up to 8192 bytes, reading each block and writing it out, then sets protection on the copy. It uses DOS file calls and a memory buffer, and it moves to a fresh stack area when the stack is low.

name: copy_name_and_lookup
description: Copies a name string into a fixed buffer, calls helpers to look it up and process it, and returns a flag that is one when the lookup succeeds and zero otherwise. When the stack is low it moves to a fresh stack area, copies a string and calls a library routine at offset minus 348 before retrying.

name: create_directory_path
description: Walks a path one component at a time, locking each directory and creating any that do not exist, using a 256-byte scratch buffer. It returns a flag that is one when the final directory is in place, and it moves to a fresh stack area when the stack is low.

name: return_immediately
description: Executes a return immediately with no other work.

name: return_immediately
description: Executes a return immediately with no other work.

name: free_install_memory_lists
description: Frees two linked lists of memory blocks by calling the library free routine at offset minus 210 on each node, and clears the head of the first list. For the second list it also restores a stack limit field from each node and calls the library routine at offset minus 732 when the version is above 35.

name: split_path_into_components
description: Splits a slash-separated path into components by writing a zero byte after each separator and recording where each component starts, for up to 16 components. It handles backslash escapes and returns zero on success or minus one when the path is empty, too long or contains a rejected character.

name: split_path_into_parts
description: Separates a path into a volume part before a colon, a directory part before the last slash, and a file-name part, copying each into the output buffers that were supplied. It also handles an extension after the last dot and returns a pointer to one of the outputs.

name: append_separator_if_missing
description: Appends the separator byte held in a global variable to a string when the string is non-empty and does not already end in a slash, colon or backslash.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from the source address to the destination address until a zero byte is copied, and returns the start of the destination.

name: convert_integer_to_string
description: Converts an integer to decimal digits by repeatedly dividing it, storing each digit as a character. It then reverses the digits into the output buffer, null-terminates it and returns the length.

name: convert_octal_to_string
description: Converts an unsigned value to octal digits by repeatedly taking its low three bits. It then reverses the digits into the output buffer, null-terminates it and returns the length.

name: convert_hex_to_string
description: Converts an unsigned value to hexadecimal digits using a lookup table of characters. It then reverses the digits into the output buffer, null-terminates it and returns the length.

name: parse_signed_integer
description: Reads a signed decimal integer from the string at the address register, including an optional sign, and stores it through the second address. It returns the number of characters consumed.

name: allocate_file_handle_record
description: Checks a flag bit in a file record and, when it is clear, calls a routine to obtain a buffer and sets the record's fields from a global value. If the buffer is missing it stores the error code twelve and returns minus one, otherwise it returns zero.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Converts each letter of a zero-terminated string to upper case in place, using a character-class table to decide which bytes are lower-case letters.

name: write_to_file_record
description: Writes data to a file record after checking the record's flags. It stores an error code and returns minus one when the record is invalid or not open for writing, and reports the DOS error code when a write fails.

name: read_text_without_carriage_returns
description: Reads from a file record into a buffer, then copies the data back in place without carriage-return bytes and returns the number of bytes kept. It stores an error code and returns minus one when the record is invalid or not open for reading.

name: read_text_without_carriage_returns
description: Reads from a file record into a buffer, then copies the data back in place without carriage-return bytes and returns the number of bytes kept. It stores an error code and returns minus one when the record is invalid or not open for reading.

name: seek_file_record
description: Seeks within a file record to the position given by the mode parameter, storing the DOS error code when the seek fails. A mode of two triggers a second seek call after a successful first one.

name: close_file_record
description: Closes a file record by calling the DOS close routine when it is open, releasing its buffers when they are present, and clearing its handle. It returns zero on success and minus one when the record is invalid or not open.

name: open_file_record
description: Adds a file record to a linked list, copies the file name into it and translates the access-mode flags into record flags. It then opens the file through the DOS lock or open calls and returns the record's index, or minus one with an error code stored when the open fails.

name: normalize_fixed_point
description: Divides a 32-bit fixed-point numerator by a denominator, shifting both according to the denominator's magnitude, and returns a 64-bit result made of the quotient and the scaled remainder. It corrects a borrow when the partial product is larger than the remainder.

name: compute_fixed_point_product
description: Multiplies two 32-bit fixed-point values by combining their 16-bit halves, cross terms and low-half product, and returns the 32-bit result.

name: return_immediately
description: Executes a return immediately with no other work.

name: close_all_file_records
description: Walks the list of open file records and closes each one that needs it, calling the DOS close routine or a stored callback depending on the record's flags. It sets a global flag first and calls one further routine at the end.

name: parse_command_line_open_streams
description: Splits the command-line text into up to 32 argument strings, honouring quotes and star escapes, then sets up the input and output streams, falling back to the NIL: device.

name: copy_text_and_run_handler
description: Copies up to 79 characters from a stored string into a local buffer and, when an output stream is open, writes it with a newline. It then calls a library routine at offset minus 348 with the buffer and stores a handler in a table slot, returning zero or the result of a follow-up call.

name: copy_text_and_run_handler
description: Copies up to 79 characters from a stored string into a local buffer and, when an output stream is open, writes it with a newline. It then calls a library routine at offset minus 348 with the buffer and stores a handler in a table slot, returning zero or the result of a follow-up call.

name: find_file_record_by_index
description: Returns the file record at the given index in the linked list, walking the list from its head. It stores error code nine when the index is out of range and error code five when the list ends early, returning zero in both cases.

name: poll_break_signal_and_respond
description: Reads the task's signal flags with the exec SetSignal routine and, when a break bit is set and the state is not one, writes the stored message to the output stream followed by a newline. It then calls the library routine at offset minus 348 and returns zero or the result of a follow-up call.

name: find_byte_in_buffer
description: Scans a buffer of the given length for a target byte and returns a pointer to the first match, or zero if the length is used up without a match.

name: append_string_to_buffer
description: Appends a zero-terminated source string to the end of a destination string, copying no more than the given count of bytes and writing a terminating zero.

name: append_string_unbounded
description: Finds the terminating zero of the destination string and copies the source string after it, including its terminator, then returns the destination address.

name: copy_string_zero_padded
description: Copies a zero-terminated source into the destination up to a count of bytes, then pads the rest of the count with zero bytes.

name: copy_byte_block_safe
description: Copies a block of the given length from source to destination, copying backwards when the regions overlap so that no bytes are lost.

name: free_pool_block
description: Frees a block previously obtained from the memory pool by locating its pool list entry, clearing its in-use bit and merging it with free neighbours. It stores error code twenty-two when the pointer is not inside any pool.

name: free_pool_block
description: Frees a block previously obtained from the memory pool by locating its pool list entry, clearing its in-use bit and merging it with free neighbours. It stores error code twenty-two when the pointer is not inside any pool.

name: allocate_pool_block
description: Allocates a block of at least the requested size from the memory pool, first searching existing pool chunks for a free region and otherwise taking a new chunk from the system. It rounds the size up to a multiple of four, stores an error code when the request is zero or the allocation fails, and returns a pointer to the block or zero.

name: allocate_pool_block
description: Allocates a block of at least the requested size from the memory pool, first searching existing pool chunks for a free region and otherwise taking a new chunk from the system. It rounds the size up to a multiple of four, stores an error code when the request is zero or the allocation fails, and returns a pointer to the block or zero.

name: run_cleanup_callbacks_then_close
description: Runs each callback in a stored list, calls a helper for the entries that need it, and sets a global flag. It then closes the open file records through the DOS close routine, or their callbacks, and finishes with a further routine call.

name: append_byte_to_buffer
description: Appends a byte to a buffer and keeps its used count in a structure field. It calls a flush routine and resets the count when the index passes 511.

name: call_and_return_flag_status
description: Calls a routine with the incoming parameter and a stack slot, then returns minus one when a flag field in a global structure has bit 4 or bit 5 set, and zero otherwise.

name: read_line_into_buffer
description: Reads characters into the buffer until a newline or the end of input, then terminates the buffer with a zero byte. It returns the buffer, or zero when nothing was read before the end of input.

name: read_next_input_byte
description: Returns the next byte from an input stream, refilling its buffer through helper calls when it is empty and recording end-of-file or error flags. It returns minus one at the end of the input or on an error, and it handles the standard-input record as a special case.

name: get_file_record_position
description: Returns the current position of a file record, adjusting for buffered data and for newline conversions in text mode. It stores error code nine and returns minus one when the record is missing.

name: get_file_record_position
description: Returns the current position of a file record, adjusting for buffered data and for newline conversions in text mode. It stores error code nine and returns minus one when the record is missing.

name: reset_file_record_buffers
description: Clears the buffer position, count and status fields of a file record, and flushes it first when a flag is set. It returns zero on success and minus one when the follow-up call fails.

name: copy_chars_into_record_buffer
description: Copies up to a count of characters from the source into a file record's buffer after checking the record's flags. It stops at the buffer limit, calls helper routines when a newline is copied in line-buffered mode, and returns the number of bytes copied or zero when the record is not writable.

name: copy_chars_into_record_buffer
description: Copies up to a count of characters from the source into a file record's buffer after checking the record's flags. It stops at the buffer limit, calls helper routines when a newline is copied in line-buffered mode, and returns the number of bytes copied or zero when the record is not writable.

name: read_bytes_from_record
description: Reads up to a requested count of bytes from a file record into a buffer, copying from its internal buffer and refilling it through helper calls. It checks the record's flags first and returns the number of bytes read, or zero when the record is not readable.

name: update_file_node_state
description: Resets the position and status fields of one file record, or when given no record, checks each record in the list. Returns zero on success, or minus one when a record reports a failure.

name: finish_file_record_close
description: Closes one file record by flushing pending output when the record is writable and then clearing its handle field. It returns minus one when the record is missing or when the flush or final close fails, and zero otherwise.
